chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz and Fadala and Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about a man who had dinars owed to him by another man, so he assigned another man in place of the debtor for the dinars. He asked: Should he take them as dirhams? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: Can a creditor accept a different currency when a debt is transferred to a new debtor?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of currency substitution within *hiwalah* (debt transfer), affirming the creditor's unilateral right to accept a different currency (dirhams for dinars) based on mutual consent or preference. It reflects the Shia juristic view that such transactions are valid provided there is no hidden usury (*riba*) or ambiguity (*gharar*), emphasizing the flexibility of commercial contracts in early Islamic jurisprudence.
